_about: Machine-readable map of the templates. tools/check_templates.py keeps it, the templates and the fixture briefs in step. 'uses' lists every placeholder a template (with its includes) can contain.

project_name.description: The project's name, as the user says it.

one_liner.description: One sentence: what it is and who it is for.

project_type.description: software, data-analysis or other (selects the variant).

size.description: lite, standard or full (how much package the project needs).

size_reason.description: One plain sentence: why this size was chosen (or that the owner chose it, and why).

owner_name.description: Who owns the plan and makes every decision in it.

audience.description: Who will use it, or read it.

success_definition.description: What success looks like, in the user's words.

out_of_scope.description: What is deliberately not being done.

systems.description: Systems, accounts and tools it connects to (or 'None').

real_world_changes.description: 'yes' or 'no', then a sentence: can it send, publish, delete or change real data?

shape.description: How the finished thing is used and kept up to date, chosen from the answers: with Claude when asked; a finished document or file; a page the team uses that Claude refreshes; Claude refreshes it on a schedule (needs Cowork); or software that runs without Claude (Cowork or Claude Code). One sentence.

shape_reason.description: Which answers led to that shape, in one sentence, so the choice can be revisited.

shape_switch_if.description: What would mean a different shape is needed (for example: it must update itself with nobody asking; people outside Claude need it; it must feed another system). Checked whenever something is added.

never_events.description: The mistakes that would be costly and must never happen.

look_and_feel.description: Look, feel and words (software), or format, audience and tone (documents, analysis).

devices.description: Devices it must work on (software only).

constraints.description: Deadlines, required or forbidden tools, budget, who reviews.

deadline.description: The date that matters most, as YYYY-MM-DD, or 'None'.

review_cadence.description: How often to pause for the user's review.

commit_policy.description: When to save snapshots of the work (never unless asked, or after each story).

comfort_level.description: How much technical detail the user wants (tunes wording only).

open_items.description: Open questions and unknowns, each to be answered early.

key_terms.description: The project's own words and what they mean.

today.description: The date the package is generated.

phases_heading.description: 'Order of work' for Lite, 'Phases' for Standard and Full.

package_files.description: The files written into this package, listed.

package_check.description: What the package check found, written after it runs (for example 'scripts/check_package.py: 0 errors, 0 warnings').
